import pandas as pd

# Define all source file paths exactly as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_90/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_90/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_90/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_90/test_3.csv"
]

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0) for file in source_files]

# All source tables share the same schema and the target schema is ['occluded'] (integer)
# The target table contains only distinct occluded values (0 and 1)
# So we concatenate all source tables and extract distinct occluded values

df_all = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Select distinct occluded values, sort them ascending, and reset index
result = df_all[['occluded']].drop_duplicates().sort_values(by='occluded').reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_90/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
